subject: Using knit2html (with brew) output in shiny

messages.author: 48f24841e806e6c6
messages.subject: Using knit2html (with brew) output in shiny
parts:
Well, as is standard operating procedure around here, I'm getting vague direction on my TeachingLab demo. I've now updated it to contain the functionality of what our users here at Vanderbilt might use.

Again, here's the link to TeachingLab running on glimmer:

http://glimmer.rstudio.com/jeffreyhorner/TeachingLab/

and github:

https://github.com/jeffreyhorner/TeachingLab

The intention is to use an Rmd file to define either a portion of or all of the shiny application interface. This gives you the niceties of both knitr/markdown plus the convenience of shiny outputs:

1. Markdown markup for headings, etc.
2. Mathjax support
3. Formatted R code with syntax highlighting
4. Shiny outputs like sliders, animation, plot outputs, etc.

The above example defines a portion of it by tying teaching.Rmd to a tab, but you could definitely do something like Yihui does in his knitr-shiny app using bootstrapPage rather than what I do with pageWithSideBar and my customHeaderPanel.

The only hitch (and maybe a hack) is that I now brew the Rmd document before handing it off to knit2html so that I can execute R commands inline to produce the shiny HTML output. Maybe I'm missing something with knitr, because I didn't see a way of doing this solely with knitr?

What do you think?

Jeff

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: Using knit2html (with brew) output in shiny
parts:
For <% %> in brew, the equivalent syntax in knitr for inline R code in
Rmd is `r `, e.g. `r mean(x)`. I guess this should help.

Regards,
Yihui
